title: Sonam Wangchuk Claims House Arrest as Ladakh Protests Winter Poll Schedule
excerpt: The climate activist says dozens of armed guards surround his Leh residence after demands to postpone the December 4 hill council elections, while police say he was advised to stay home under prohibitory orders.
body:
• Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk says he is under house arrest in Leh, claiming dozens of armed guards surround his residence while officials say he was advised to stay at home.
  • The administration has notified elections for eight Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils, with polling scheduled for December 4.
  • Wangchuk and his associates are demanding the release of the Judicial Enquiry Commission report on last year's killings in Leh, alongside postponement of the winter polls.
  • Police removed Wangchuk from a protest site on Wednesday and escorted him home, citing prohibitory orders that ban rallies and gatherings within Leh Municipality limits.

Ladakhi climate activist Sonam Wangchuk has claimed that authorities have placed him under house arrest in Leh after he and other regional representatives demanded the postponement of the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (LAHDC) elections scheduled for December, IANS reported.

Taking to social media platform X, Wangchuk stated that dozens of armed guards had been deployed around his residence, disputing official claims that he was merely advised to remain indoors.

"I AM UNDER HOUSE ARREST. Dozens of armed guards surround my house while the government version says 'I have been advised to stay at home'."

In the same post, quoted by IANS, he asked why the Judicial Enquiry Commission report on last year's killings in Leh is delayed and described the council election as a "phoney" poll "foisted on people with rocket speed in mid-winter". He further alleged that the entire region of Ladakh is protesting and claimed that the reach of his X, Instagram and YouTube accounts had been drastically suppressed.

The official account

Ladakh Police have given a different description of the same events. According to The CSR Journal, police removed Wangchuk from his protest site in Leh on Wednesday, escorting him to his residence, and said the preventive measure was taken in compliance with directives issued by the Chief Electoral Officer of the Union Territory of Ladakh and the District Magistrate of Leh. The prohibitory orders specifically ban public rallies, protests and other gatherings within the Leh Municipality limits, and police advised Wangchuk to remain at home to ensure compliance.

Authorities said such actions were necessary to prevent any potential breach of public order and to maintain peace, and urged the public to adhere to the restrictions in light of the upcoming Panchayat, Municipal and LAHDC elections.

In a video message accompanying his post, Wangchuk said that the previous evening people calling themselves policemen told his group they should not move out, and that after he told the personnel he was prepared to be arrested, they escorted him to his institute, where his residence is also located, and instructed him not to leave the premises. "Dozens of policemen have been placed around to enforce my house arrest. Authorities are publicly saying that I have been advised to remain at home as a prohibitory measure," he said, according to IANS.

Why the winter schedule is opposed

The administration has notified elections for eight LAHDCs, with polling scheduled for December 4. Wangchuk and local leaders have strongly opposed the winter schedule, saying extreme cold forces a large part of the population, including students, to temporarily relocate outside the region in December, IANS reported.

In his video appeal, titled "Ladakh's SOS Appeal to the Nation" and addressed to President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah, Wangchuk noted that December and January are typically the coldest and snowiest months in Ladakh, with temperatures often dropping below minus 30 degrees Celsius, and claimed nearly half of the local population migrates out of the region during this period for education, holidays and pilgrimage, according to The CSR Journal. He also alleged that discussions aimed at restoring democracy in the Union Territory had stalled.

What happens next

Wangchuk said peaceful dharnas were held the previous day and would continue the next day so that the demands are accepted, according to IANS. The CSR Journal reported that leaders from both Leh and Kargil, including the local Member of Parliament, have united in calls for intervention, and that Wangchuk warned the community might be compelled to initiate peaceful but intense protests if their concerns are not addressed. For now, the election schedule stands as notified, the prohibitory orders remain in force in Leh, and the two sides describe Wangchuk's confinement in incompatible terms: house arrest, in his words, or advice to stay home, in the police's.
nri_angle: The dispute over Ladakh's winter polls and Wangchuk's confinement is a major governance story for readers in India and the diaspora following the region.
author: Diaspora Desk
